title: Injective model for global sections of the closed support object
statement:
Fix a finite commutative ring $A$. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes with quasi-compact complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Work with ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] and their derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], with exact $i_*$ and $i^*,j^*$ as in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Put $i^!_0M=i^*\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$ [def-pur-flasque-support], and write $S=Ri^!_0$ on $D^+$, with its support counit $\epsilon:i_*SK\to K$ as in [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle]. The sheaf functor $i^!_0$ is right adjoint to the exact sheaf functor $i_*$ and preserves injective objects. For every bounded-below complex of injective $A_X$-module sheaves $I$ representing $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, the complex $i^!_0I$ is bounded below and termwise injective, represents $SK$, and computes its derived global sections. There is an equality of complexes, natural in chain maps of such representatives,
$$\Gamma(Z,i^!_0I)=\Gamma(X,i_*i^!_0I)=\ker\bigl(I(X)\to I(U)\bigr)=\Gamma_Z(X,I),$$
with all differentials induced by those of $I$. Consequently it induces a canonical natural isomorphism
$$R\Gamma(Z,SK)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_Z(X,K)$$
in the derived category of $A$-modules. Here $\Gamma_Z$ is the kernel-of-restriction functor and $R\Gamma_Z$ its bounded-below right derived functor [def-pur-support-cohomology]; the isomorphism in degree $r\in\mathbf Z$ is an isomorphism of cohomology modules, not an identification with a sheaf.

proof.text: Use the existing ordinary module-valued pro-etale sheaf Grothendieck instance of [lem-sfb-proetale-sheaves-grothendieck] and enough injectives [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] on the small site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The additive functors and derived categories in the statement are already published with this presentation; no transport to intrinsic ringed-site modules is needed.

Let G be finiteSupportedSections, the kernel of the open adjunction unit. Any map i_*N to M has zero composite with that unit: transpose along the open adjunction, and use the empty-fibre vanishing of open restriction of a disjoint direct image [lem-sfb-proetale-open-disjoint-direct-image]. Evaluating the functor-category kernel at M preserves its universal property. Factor the map uniquely through G(M), compose with the canonical invertible comparison G(M) to i_*i^!_0(M) of [def-pur-flasque-support], then use full faithfulness [lem-exc-proetale-closed-fully-faithful]. The inverse Hom equivalence is i_* applied to the map followed by the inverse-comparison kernel inclusion. Naturality of this inclusion proves the two naturality conditions of Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv, and its value on the identity gives exactly supportModelInclusion as counit.

source.place: Tag 09XQ (lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic, Hom argument); proetale.tex Tags 09AA (lemma-closed-immersion), 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open), ordinary module version

proof.text: Closed direct image preserves finite limits because it is right adjoint to ordinary inverse image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], so it preserves monomorphisms. Apply [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] to the sheaf adjunction of step 2. This proves that i^!_0 preserves injectives; finite-colimit preservation is not needed for this inference. Its additivity and the general map_isStrictlySupported instance preserve every given lower bound of a complex.

source.place: Tag 09XQ (lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic, exactness and injectivity argument); proetale.tex Tag 09BM (lemma-closed-immersion-complement-retrocompact-exact)

proof.text: For each bounded-below homotopy complex I of injectives, the terms of i^!_0(I) are injective by step 3. The injective right-derivability instance of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] makes the derived unit for i^!_0 invertible on I, and the derived global-section unit invertible on its image. The same instance makes the supported-section derived unit invertible on I. These are precisely all three model-computation clauses in the statement.

Apply the explicit injectivity-and-range section formula of [def-pur-flasque-support] at the terminal object X. The fibre-product projection for j differs from the canonical restriction to i.openComplement only by an isomorphism of site objects: use pullback.snd for the terminal base change and the isomorphism between open immersions with equal ranges. The sheaf sends this isomorphism to an isomorphism, so the two restriction maps vanish on exactly the same sections, including the empty-scheme cases. ModuleCat.isLimitKernelFork therefore identifies G(M)(X) with the actual categorical kernel defining [def-pur-support-cohomology], compatibly with its inclusion. Kernel cancellation and naturality of the sheaf kernel inclusion make this isomorphism natural in M. Compose it with evaluation of global sections, the inverse supported-closed comparison, and the direct-image global-section isomorphism of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Naturality of global-section evaluation gives exactly the displayed counit normalization.

source.place: Tag 09XP (section-cohomology-support, definitions of supported sections and supported subsheaf); ordinary pro-etale module version

proof.text: Apply the proved bounded-below composition theorem Functor.rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompIso' from WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.RightDerivedFunctor.PlusComp to i^!_0, global sections on Z, and the natural isomorphism c of step 5 with the supported-section functor [def-pur-support-cohomology]. Its only extra hypothesis is preservation of injectives, already proved in step 3. It gives the desired e with no further support-theoretic lemma. The theorem is obtained from the injective right-derivability and uniqueness universal properties of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective].

The composition theorem's rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompIso'_fac is a natural-transformation identity on all bounded-below homotopy complexes. Evaluate it at I. The composition map Functor.mapHomotopyCategoryPlusCompIso c agrees with NatTrans.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus c.hom: apply the faithful inclusion in the ambient homotopy category, represent I there by a cochain complex, and both sides are definitionally the quotient of the same termwise chain map. Reassociate the composite unit using rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompUnit_app. This is the exact final equation of the statement. Thus naturality and representative independence come from the general derived-functor construction, without a separate K-injective Hom argument. Apply any homology functor to obtain the asserted cohomology isomorphisms.

Statement: identical to the base except one repaired citation. def-weil-pbc-derived-categories is étale-only, so replacing it with def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-abstract-derived-category and def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories is correct and changes no hypothesis or conclusion. S=Ri^!_0 is the same functor as in lem-pur-support-localization-triangle. Source: I read Stacks 09XQ (etale-cohomology.tex l.14023, Hom formula and exact i_*) and 09XP (l.13966, Γ_Z = ker(I(X)→I(U))); the pro-étale adaptation is honestly marked agent. Steps: Step 1 gives Grothendieck and enough injectives for any ring sheaf; the constant sheaf equals (Cont(π0,A))^# for finite A. Step 2 is correct: η∘f has adjunct j^*f, which is 0 since j^*i_*=0; q is the qc-j iso of def-pur-flasque-support; closed-fully-faithful gives full faithfulness; the counit is q^{-1} followed by the inclusion. Step 3 is the Mathlib leaf for right adjoints of exact functors. Steps 4 and 6 use clause (2) of right-derived-plus-injective three times, with composites in the correct direction. Step 5's sectionwise identification uses the direct-image formula and the explicit kernel formula. Step 7's lift and representative independence uses K-injective Hom bijections and is written out, not hand-waved. Small cases checked: Z=∅, Z=X, X1⊔X2, negative shifts; no Noetherian hypothesis is needed. No cycle; nothing cites a dropped node; no SGA. I accept the 3 tool_uses (ring-sheaves-grothendieck, proetale-ringed-open-closed, exc-proetale-closed-fully-faithful) as generic tools. Overlap: lem-exc-proetale-derived-adjunction-triangle and lem-exc-proetale-closed-support prove a similar adjunction but only for Noetherian T, so they are not duplicates of this arbitrary-X item. Advisory: the i^{-1}i_*≅id clause of ringed-open-closed would make the third tool use unnecessary. No fixes.
